dossier.purpose: Python CLI (`tvly`, package `tavily-cli` 0.1.9, pyproject.toml:6-7) for Tavily's hosted web-data service: search, extract, crawl, map, deep research and feedback commands with Rich or `--json` output, plus `tvly init`, which authenticates and installs Tavily's eight agent skills for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor (README.md:3, 12, 85-91). The repo has no page-fetching, HTML/PDF-parsing or browser code; each command builds a kwargs dict and calls a remote client (e.g. `client.extract(**kwargs)`, tavily_cli/commands/extract.py:74). Need coverage: (1) Fetch chosen URLs and extract main text with metadata: `tvly extract <url>...` (max 20 URLs per call, extract.py:42,51-52; options --query, --chunks-per-source, --extract-depth basic|advanced, --format markdown|text, --include-images, --timeout, -o; extract.py:19-25) is shell-callable. The CLI reads, per URL, `url` + `raw_content`, plus `failed_results[].url/error` and `response_time` (tavily_cli/output.py:187-218). Page metadata beyond those fields (title, author, publish date, etc.) is not referenced anywhere in this repo; whatever else is returned is defined by the remote API/tavily-python SDK, which is not in this repo and was not read. (2) Bounded interaction with JavaScript-rendered pages (forms, sign-in, tabs, screenshots, PDF): no such command or code exists in this repo (repo-wide search for playwright/selenium/puppeteer/screenshot/pdf/chromium/webdriver/cookie found nothing; the only JS-related feature is the server-side `--extract-depth advanced` option, README.md:212-213).

claims.claim: CLI and agent tools for the Tavily API: search, extract, crawl, map and research from the command line; the package provides the `tvly` command and depends on the official `tavily-python` SDK.

Content Extraction: 'Extract clean markdown from any URL'; `tvly extract` takes several URLs, optional `--query`, `--extract-depth basic|advanced`, `--format markdown|text`, `--include-images`, `--timeout` (1-60 s), `-o`.
'Advanced extraction for JS-heavy pages' is `tvly extract https://spa-app.com --extract-depth advanced`.
`tvly search` and `tvly extract` run without sign-in using keyless access with a fair-use rate-limit cap; `crawl`, `map`, `research` and `feedback` require authentication.
`--output` writes the structured JSON response regardless of file extension; `--format markdown` only controls content inside that response; `crawl --output-dir` saves each page as a Markdown file.
CLI for humans and AI agents: Rich output for humans, `--json` for agents; every command supports `--json`; `-` reads input from stdin for search and research.
Exit codes: 0 success; 1 local setup/update error; 2 usage error; 3 auth failure, keyless cap or handled plan limit; 4 API error, setup live-search failure or update-check error.

`tvly init` detects Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, installs Tavily's eight core agent skills into `~/.agents/skills` (exposed to the selected agents), then verifies with a live search; no Node.js required.
Browser OAuth uses Tavily's MCP endpoint and has known compatibility gaps; API-key authentication is needed for the full option set, streaming, structured output and async research.
Setup always performs a live search, so it needs network access even with `--skip-skills`.
Requires Python 3.10+; install via guided curl|sh installer, uv, pipx, pip or from source; `tvly update` updates through the originating package manager.
Environment variables: `TAVILY_API_KEY` (highest priority, no login needed) and `TAVILY_HUMAN_ID` (optional identifier attached to every request for usage attribution).
`--include-domains` restricts search to listed domains (example sec.gov,reuters.com); `--client-name` sets `client_name` 'for attribution'.

install.command:
git clone https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-cli.git
cd tavily-cli
pip install -e .

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README names no OS, but pyproject declares 'Operating System :: OS Independent' (pyproject.toml:20), the wheel is pure Python (pyproject.toml:56-57), Python >=3.10 (pyproject.toml:10), and installer/code special-case Linux display detection (install.sh:51-54, tavily_cli/oauth.py:413). No CI exists, so there is no upstream test-run evidence on Linux.
platforms.wsl2: unknown - README and code never mention WSL (repo-wide search: no matches). On WSL sys.platform is 'linux' and, without DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY, looks_headless() is true (tavily_cli/oauth.py:406-415), so no browser is auto-opened; the --no-browser OAuth flow still needs a 127.0.0.1 callback reachable from the browser (README.md:157-161). `tvly login --api-key` or TAVILY_API_KEY avoids the callback (README.md:145-148).
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - same basis as Linux: OS-independent pure-Python package (pyproject.toml:20, 56-57), nothing architecture-specific in the code, installer's only OS branch is Linux (install.sh:51). README names no OS and there is no CI or test evidence on macOS.
platforms.gpu: no - not used or needed; no local model or inference code, all processing is remote (tavily_cli/mcp_client.py:16; README.md:3).

integrations.cli: Yes - `tvly` console script (pyproject.toml:47-48) with subcommands init, login, logout, auth, search, extract, crawl, map, research [run|status|poll], feedback, update; no subcommand opens an interactive REPL; `--json` structured output, `--version`, `--status`, documented exit codes (tavily_cli/cli.py:19-55, 161-171; README.md:296-313, 358-366).
integrations.mcp: No MCP server is provided (none found). The CLI is a client of Tavily's hosted remote MCP endpoint https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp, used only when the credential is an OAuth JWT: JSON-RPC tools/call for tavily_search, tavily_extract, tavily_crawl, tavily_map, tavily_research, tavily_get_research and tavily_feedback (tavily_cli/mcp_client.py:16, 33-75, 137-156; tavily_cli/config.py:538-545; README.md:163-165).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No documented Python library API: tavily_cli/__init__.py only defines __version__. The CLI depends on the tavily-python SDK (>=0.7.25, pyproject.toml:30; README.md:5-6) and uses tavily.TavilyClient for API-key and keyless calls (tavily_cli/config.py:546-572) against Tavily's hosted API (api.tavily.com per tavily_cli/mcp_client.py:3-6). The base URL can be overridden through TAVILY_API_BASE_URL or config api_base_url, which the README does not document (config.py:277-283). `feedback` posts to {base_url}/feedback through the SDK session (feedback.py:50-55). Tavily API docs are at https://docs.tavily.com (README.md:3); not fetched.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Yes, via skills: `tvly init --agent claude-code|codex|cursor` (or `--all`, `--yes`) installs eight Tavily skills (tavily-best-practices, tavily-cli, tavily-crawl, tavily-dynamic-search, tavily-extract, tavily-map, tavily-research, tavily-search) from tavily-ai/skills@ea5e8201b0d3ed9c10b70b71187589bd761fe2d2 into ~/.agents/skills. It links them into ~/.claude/skills, ~/.codex/skills and ~/.cursor/skills, honoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME (README.md:85-91, 93-115; tavily_cli/init_skills.py:17-30, 56-74, 100-157). The skill contents live in a separate repo and were not read. This repo contains no plugin manifest, MCP server config or hooks; .gitignore:33 only ignores a local .claude/ directory.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No analytics/telemetry code: a repo-wide search for telemetry/analytics/sentry/posthog/mixpanel/opentelemetry and similar terms found nothing. No automatic update check or background call was found in cli.py; PyPI is contacted only by `tvly update` (tavily_cli/commands/update.py:37-47). Every Tavily request does carry identifiers by design: a per-terminal/agent session ID derived from the parent/grandparent PID and persisted in ~/.tavily/session.json (config.py:50-97), `client_source` ('tavily-cli' or 'tavily-cli-keyless'), optional `client_name`, and optional `human_id` from TAVILY_HUMAN_ID or config (config.py:266-274, 535-572). The MCP path sends them as headers x-client-source, x-client-name, mcp-session-id, X-Session-Id and X-Human-Id (mcp_client.py:52-67). Network endpoints: Tavily API via tavily-python (api.tavily.com per mcp_client.py:3-6); https://mcp.tavily.com for OAuth discovery/registration/token/revoke and MCP JSON-RPC (oauth.py:27-42, mcp_client.py:16); https://pypi.org/pypi/tavily-cli/json (update.py:23-24); https://codeload.github.com/tavily-ai/skills/tar.gz/<pinned commit> (only for `tvly init` with skills, init_skills.py:17-20). `tvly init` always runs a live search, even with --skip-skills (init.py:97-104; README.md:332-334). Accounts: none for keyless search/extract, which are rate-capped (README.md:117-130; config.py:557-572); a Tavily API key or Tavily OAuth login is required for crawl/map/research/feedback (crawl.py:55-60, map_cmd.py:45-51, research.py:155-168, feedback.py:89-98). URLs and queries passed to extract/search are sent to Tavily (extract.py:74). Credential resolution can refresh OAuth tokens over the network (config.py:443-475), including for `tvly auth` and `tvly --status`. Local state: ~/.tavily/config.json (0600, dir 0700; config.py:152-187), ~/.tavily/session.json (config.py:84-91), ~/.mcp-auth/ read and cleaned for Tavily tokens (config.py:354-389), skills under ~/.agents/skills (init_skills.py:117). OAuth login opens a loopback HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1 (random port, 180 s timeout; oauth.py:33, 452-476).

entry_points.what: click group `cli`; wires login/logout/auth/init/search/extract/crawl/map/research/feedback/update; no subcommand launches the REPL
`tvly extract` - up to 20 URLs per call, keyless fallback, forwards options to client.extract
`tvly search` - supports --include-raw-content, domain/date filters, stdin query via '-'
`tvly init` - auth, skills install for claude-code/codex/cursor, CLI check, live search
Guided POSIX installer; prefers uv, then pipx, then pip; hands off to `tvly init` on fresh interactive desktop installs
run_repl - interactive shell that dispatches into the click group
McpTavilyClient - JSON-RPC client for https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp, used for OAuth credentials

code.architecture: Thin click-based client. cli.py defines the `tvly` group and imports one module per command in tavily_cli/commands/ (search, extract, crawl, map_cmd, research, feedback, init, auth, update). Commands assemble optional kwargs and call a client chosen in config.py (get_client / get_client_or_keyless): tavily.TavilyClient from the tavily-python SDK for tvly-* keys and for keyless mode, or mcp_client.McpTavilyClient (JSON-RPC tools/call to https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp) when the credential is an OAuth JWT. config.py also holds credential precedence (env > api_key > OAuth in ~/.tavily/config.json > legacy ~/.mcp-auth), file locking, session IDs and optional human_id/base URL. oauth.py implements native OAuth 2.1 + PKCE with dynamic client registration and a 127.0.0.1 callback. output.py renders Rich or JSON and sanitizes untrusted text via common.sanitize_control; common.py holds error/exit-code handling; keyless.py renders the keyless-cap envelope; init_skills.py downloads, checksum-verifies and installs the eight skills; commands/update.py detects pip/pipx/uv installs and shells out to the manager; repl.py is the interactive shell; theme.py is branding and spinner. All page fetching and extraction happens on the remote service; the repo contains no fetcher, parser or browser code.
code.packaging_and_release: Build backend hatchling (pyproject.toml:1-3); wheel packages `tavily_cli` only (pyproject.toml:56-57); sdist includes tavily_cli, tests, install.sh, pyproject.toml, README.md and LICENSE (pyproject.toml:59-67); distributed on PyPI as `tavily-cli` (README.md:41-48; update.py:23-24). Version 0.1.9 (pyproject.toml:7); no git tag is visible in this shallow clone (.git/packed-refs lists only refs/remotes/origin/main; .git/shallow present). No release or publish workflow, checksums, signatures, SBOM or attestations exist in the repository (no .github/ directory; glob for .github/** is empty). The only integrity control in code is the skills archive, pinned to a commit and verified by SHA-256 (init_skills.py:17-20, 92-93). install.sh is fetched from the main branch and installs from PyPI via uv/pipx/pip without hash pinning (README.md:28; install.sh:137-175).
code.tests_and_ci: pytest (dev extra, pyproject.toml:50-54). 5 test files in tests/: test_cli.py (3 tests), test_init.py (12), test_install_sh.py (10), test_oauth.py (36), test_update.py (29) = 90 `def test_` functions by grep; parametrization adds cases. Tests use click CliRunner, httpx.MockTransport, monkeypatch and pty-driven stub binaries for install.sh. Covered: CLI help and REPL text, `tvly init` and skills install/verify, install.sh behaviours, OAuth/config storage, update and install-method detection. A grep of tests/ finds no tests for the extract, crawl, map, research or feedback commands, output.py, sanitize_control or mcp_client.py. No CI: no .github/ directory and no other workflow, tox, nox or Makefile files in the repo. Ruff is configured (pyproject.toml:69-75) but nothing runs it automatically. Tests were not run for this dossier; counts are from static search.
code.dependencies: pyproject.toml:29-39 lists 9 direct runtime dependencies: tavily-python>=0.7.25, click>=8.1.0, rich>=13.0.0, httpx>=0.27.0, packaging>=23.2, requests>=2.32.4, urllib3>=2.2.2, certifi>=2024.7.4, psutil>=5.9.0. requests, urllib3 and certifi are not imported anywhere in tavily_cli/ (grep), so they are declared but not used directly. Dev extra (pyproject.toml:50-54): pytest>=8.0.0, ruff>=0.4.0. Build requires hatchling (pyproject.toml:2). No lockfile or requirements*.txt exists. Transitive dependencies of tavily-python cannot be enumerated from this repo.
code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md (and no .github/ directory). Not a policy, but in-code hardening exists: terminal-escape stripping of web/API-derived text (common.py:14-30, output.py:1-9); 0600/0700 permissions and atomic, flock-serialized config writes (config.py:139-187); OAuth PKCE S256, state check, HTTPS-only and issuer-pinned metadata (oauth.py:81-87, 107-132, 486-487); skills archive caps (25 MB total / 5 MB per file), SHA-256 pin, path/symlink rejection, no exec bits, scripts never executed (init_skills.py:32-33, 77-97, 178-226).

claim_checks.claim: Extract clean markdown from any URL (README.md:14; `--format markdown|text`, README.md:433)
claim_checks.evidence: Option wiring is confirmed: `--format` markdown|text (extract.py:22) and the URL list are forwarded to the remote call `client.extract(**kwargs)` (extract.py:54-74). The repo has no local fetching or parsing code, so extraction quality, 'any URL' coverage and which metadata is returned are server-side and not checkable here. The CLI reads only results[].url/raw_content, failed_results[].url/error and response_time (output.py:187-218). The terminal view prints at most 3,000 characters per page (output.py:204); `--json`/`-o` emits the full response (output.py:96-108, 183-185). Code reading only, nothing executed.

claim_checks.claim: Advanced extraction for JS-heavy pages: `tvly extract <url> --extract-depth advanced` (README.md:212-213)
claim_checks.evidence: The option exists and is forwarded (extract.py:21, 59-60). Whether JavaScript is rendered is server-side behaviour and not checkable here. Nothing in the repo provides interactive browsing: the command list is init/login/logout/auth/search/extract/crawl/map/research/feedback/update (cli.py:161-171), and a repo-wide search for playwright/selenium/puppeteer/screenshot/pdf/chromium/webdriver/cookie found only OAuth 'headless' detection (oauth.py:406-415).

claim_checks.claim: search/extract work without credentials via keyless access with a rate-limit cap; crawl, map, research and feedback require authentication (README.md:119-130)
claim_checks.evidence: config.py:557-572 builds a key-less TavilyClient when no credential resolves; extract.py:47,72,75-76 and search.py:65,107,110-111 handle TavilyKeylessLimitError (common.py:42-77, exit 3). crawl.py:60, map_cmd.py:50, research.py:167 and feedback.py:98 call require_api_key_friendly (config.py:575-605). The cap itself is enforced remotely; only its rendering is client-side. Code/README difference: README.md:502 says feedback 'Requires a Tavily API key', but require_api_key_friendly accepts any resolved credential including OAuth (config.py:575-587), and feedback routes OAuth credentials to MCP `tavily_feedback` (feedback.py:129-130).

claim_checks.claim: Extract limits: `--chunks-per-source` 1-5 (requires `--query`), `--timeout` 1-60 s (README.md:431, 435); crawl `--allow-external` default true (README.md:454)
claim_checks.evidence: Only a 20-URL cap is enforced locally (extract.py:51-52); it is stated in the command docstring (extract.py:42) but not in the README. The 1-5 and 1-60 ranges and the --query dependency appear only in help text (extract.py:20, 24) and are forwarded unvalidated (extract.py:57-58, 65-66); enforcement, if any, is in the SDK/server (not read). crawl `--allow-external/--no-external` defaults to None and is sent only when given (crawl.py:23, 86-87), so 'default: true' is a server-side default.

claim_checks.claim: `--output` writes the structured JSON response regardless of file extension; `--format markdown` only affects content inside it (README.md:282-284)
claim_checks.evidence: print_extract_results routes both --json and -o through emit() (output.py:182-185), which json.dumps the full response to the file (output.py:96-106). Crawl is the only command that writes Markdown files (--output-dir; output.py:274-297, each file starting with `# <url>`).

claim_checks.claim: `tvly init` detects Claude Code, Codex and Cursor and installs eight core skills into ~/.agents/skills, exposed to the selected agents; no Node.js (README.md:85-91, 111)
claim_checks.evidence: init_skills.py:21-30 lists exactly eight skills; 56-74 define and detect agent dirs (~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, honoring CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CODEX_HOME); 117-147 install into ~/.agents/skills and symlink into each agent's skills dir (copy fallback at 288-293). The download is plain httpx from codeload.github.com, pinned to commit ea5e8201... and SHA-256 checked (17-20, 77-97), with no Node.js involved. The skill contents are in the separate tavily-ai/skills repo and were not read.

claim_checks.claim: `--json` for agents; every command supports `--json`; stdin via '-' for search/research (README.md:12, 337-345)
claim_checks.evidence: json_option is applied to search/extract/crawl/map/feedback/init/update (e.g. extract.py:27; common.py:100-110); research run/status/poll and login/logout/auth define their own --json (research.py:132,276,313; auth.py:29,190,255); group-level --json at cli.py:22. Stdin '-' is implemented for search (search.py:68-69) and research (research.py:162-163) but extract has no stdin handling; the README does not claim it for extract. In --json mode API errors print {error: ...} to stdout (common.py:127-131).

Exit 3: keyless cap, OAuth refresh failure and 429/432 limits (common.py:54,77,90,97,154), missing key (config.py:525,605), init auth failure (init.py:68). Exit 4: API errors (common.py:131,157), init live-search failure (init.py:101,104), update-check failure (update.py:46). Exit 1: init skills/cli failures (init.py:89,94), update install/verify failures (update.py:51,66,84,90,104). Exit 2: click.UsageError (e.g. extract.py:52). Code reading only.

claim_checks.claim: Browser OAuth goes through Tavily's MCP endpoint and has known compatibility gaps; use an API key for the full option set, streaming, structured output and async research (README.md:163-165, 244-245)
claim_checks.evidence: OAuth JWT credentials select McpTavilyClient (config.py:538-545), which POSTs JSON-RPC tools/call to https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp (mcp_client.py:16, 33-75, 112-156). By code reading, `research --stream` iterates the client's return value as an SSE stream (research.py:185-209) while McpTavilyClient.research returns a parsed dict (mcp_client.py:149-150), so streaming yields nothing under OAuth, consistent with the README advice. Issue #24 (README.md:165) is outside the working directory and was not opened.

This is request/usage attribution sent to Tavily, not source citation: client_name is passed to TavilyClient (config.py:547-554, 563-571) or sent as the x-client-name header on the MCP path (mcp_client.py:58-59); TAVILY_HUMAN_ID is the analogous per-request identifier (config.py:266-274; README.md:523-524). Source attribution in outputs is by per-result `url` (output.py:191-197, 211-214), research `sources` with title/url (output.py:349, 378-381) and `--citation-format numbered|mla|apa|chicago` (research.py:128).

risks: Scope gap for page interaction: no forms, sign-in flows, tabs, screenshots or PDF commands and no browser-automation code; the command set is search/extract/crawl/map/research/feedback plus setup (tavily_cli/cli.py:161-171; README.md:296-313). The only JS-related feature is the server-side `--extract-depth advanced` (extract.py:21; README.md:212-213).

Retrieval happens on Tavily's servers, not locally: URLs and queries are sent to the service (extract.py:74), extract exposes no cookie/header/session options (extract.py:17-26), and pages needing the user's network or logged-in session are not addressable through it. Keyless search/extract is rate-capped (README.md:119-130); other commands need a Tavily key or OAuth login (crawl.py:55-60).

Output schema and metadata are not defined in this repo: extract fields come from the remote API/tavily-python (not read). The CLI references only url, raw_content, failed_results[].url/error and response_time (output.py:187-218). The terminal view prints at most 3,000 characters per page (output.py:204), so agents need `--json` or `-o` for the full payload (output.py:96-108, 183-185). README ranges (chunks 1-5, timeout 1-60) are not validated by the CLI (extract.py:20, 24, 57-66).

Weak assurance signals: no CI, release workflow, checksums, signatures or attestations; no SECURITY.md; no lockfile; pre-1.0 version 0.1.9 with 'Development Status :: 4 - Beta' (pyproject.toml:7, 17). The 90 test functions in 5 files do not exercise extract, crawl, map, research, feedback, output.py or mcp_client.py (grep of tests/).

Install/setup trust surface: README recommends `curl ... | sh` from the main branch (README.md:28); install.sh is unpinned and installs from PyPI without hash pinning (install.sh:137-175). `tvly init` writes third-party skill content from tavily-ai/skills (pinned commit + SHA-256, init_skills.py:17-20, 92-93) into ~/.agents/skills and the ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.cursor skill dirs (init_skills.py:56-69, 117-147). Those skills steer agent behaviour and were not reviewed (separate repo), including `tavily-dynamic-search` (init_skills.py:25).

Credential and identity handling: OAuth access/refresh tokens (and client_secret when issued) are stored as plaintext JSON in ~/.tavily/config.json, mode 0600 (config.py:195-210, 167-187); legacy ~/.mcp-auth/**/*_tokens.json is scanned for Tavily tokens (config.py:354-366). Every request carries a persistent per-terminal/agent session ID, client_source and optional human_id/client_name (config.py:50-97, 535-572; mcp_client.py:52-67); no opt-out for the session ID or client_source was found.

OAuth/MCP path and config caveats: the README itself warns of compatibility gaps under OAuth (README.md:163-165); by code reading `research --stream` yields nothing useful with an OAuth credential (research.py:185-209 vs mcp_client.py:149-150). The undocumented TAVILY_API_BASE_URL can redirect SDK traffic (config.py:277-283). `tavily-python>=0.7.25` has no upper bound (pyproject.toml:30) and carries the keyless and response behaviour this CLI depends on.

Service and licensing scope: MIT covers the CLI code only (LICENSE:1-21; pyproject.toml:11); the hosted service's terms, its plan limits (HTTP 429/432 handled at common.py:123-154) and the licenses of dependencies such as tavily-python were not examined. Maintenance cadence is not assessable here: the clone is shallow (.git/shallow) and no tags are visible (.git/packed-refs).
